touches.text: A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.
The instance is a number; a singleton is 0. A bare name addresses instance 0 (`cc` means `cc 0`); the number is written only when it isn't 0.
A device owns its state: only the device writes under its own ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ tree.

Ownership. The librarian owns every tree and delegates some to the devices that learn. EVERYTHING THAT LEARNS USING OUR GRAPH TREES IS A DELEGATE (CodeMother, chart and any learning block are examples, not a list), and each holds its trees by the librarian's delegation (Law 6: delegation through the owner's gate). WHY: two holders with different weights over the same nodes have different perspectives and can debate points, and the librarian, asked anything, can look at the query from both.

Cairn owns everything about the system that is Cairn and hasn't been delegated elsewhere. A delegated domain belongs to its device, not to Cairn, even though it is of Cairn: the librarian is delegated learning, research and answering queries on what's learned; the embeddings device is delegated producing the embeddings we search with. The OS and hardware belong to Recovery (6.6).

The only way to the inference host; anything that goes around it is an error. WHY: its two points are to find the cheapest model powerful enough for each request, and to train the graph trees on the results.
Device name on the command line and bus: inference.
VERBS: infer, embed, resolve, calls. COMMANDS: cairn inference show.

conflicts.text: Device name on the command line and bus: inference.
conflicts.ticket_says: The bus device name becomes 'inferenceproxy' (Decision D1: 'the bus id (device.py, shim.py)' becomes 'inferenceproxy')
conflicts.why: Outline 11.4.2 explicitly states 'Device name on the command line and bus: inference.' The ticket changes the bus device name to 'inferenceproxy' rather than keeping it as 'inference'. This is reinforced by 11.4.9 which shows the command as 'cairn inference show' — implying the bus name should be 'inference', not 'inferenceproxy'. Both cannot stand: either the bus name stays 'inference' (keeping 11.4.2 as written) or the outline must be updated to specify 'inferenceproxy' as the bus device name.
